title: AIEvent
description: The message the Java backend publishes to RabbitMQ and the Python AI service consumes. This file is the single definition of that wire format: both sides are tested against it, so neither can change it alone. Produced by com.skillbridge.shared.messaging.AIEvent; consumed by skillbridge-ai-service/main.py::_process_rabbitmq_message.

eventType.description: Which handler runs. The consumer dispatches on this exact string and skips anything it does not recognise, so adding a value here without adding a handler means the event is acknowledged and discarded.

studentId.description: The student this event is about.

collegeId.description: Tenant discriminator. NOTE: the Python consumer does not currently read this field, so AI analysis is not tenant-scoped. It is required here because the producer always sends it and scoping the consumer is Phase 12 work; dropping it from the wire now would make that harder.

metadata.description: Optional per-event detail. MUST be an object or null, never a scalar. The consumer calls .get() on it, so a bare number raises AttributeError, the message is nacked with requeue=false, and the event is discarded -- which is exactly what SKILL_UPDATED did before this contract existed.

skillId.description: Set by SKILL_UPDATED: which skill changed.

skills.description: Optional pre-resolved skill names. When absent the consumer falls back to reading them from the database.
